pr_title: Allow localhost with a port by default in development
pr_body:
Only "localhost" and ".localhost" were allowed by default in
development, but the port is also part of the header that is sent.  It
is a bad idea to try parsing whatever stuff is in the HTTP header, so
this commit specifically adds localhost with a port in the "allowed
hosts" list in development.

Fixes: #43864

comments: I'm sure I've somehow done something wonky with my setup... but this repro case is so tiny I cannot for the life of me figure out what. 😅

You haven't done something wrong. If you downgrade to rc1 it works fine.

To downgrade change your Gemfile from `gem "rails", "~> 7.0.0.rc2"` to `gem "rails", "7.0.0.rc1"`.

I suspect the issue is in https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/0fccfb9a3097a9c4260c791f1a40b128517e7815, @tenderlove does this sound likely to you too?
@ghiculescu ya, I think so.  I'm trying to make a fix

Hi all, 
also the version 6.1.4.2 has the same commit and the same problem.
Thanks a lot

cc @tenderlove
I'm waiting on CI but once it finishes I'll ship new versions of 7.0, 6.1, and 6.0.  Sorry for the disruption!
All new gems should be pushed!

@tenderlove Thanks for the fix and speed to resolve. My app is still broken in development though, as I use the hosts files to access my app locally on different domains (eg, to test different country domains or multi-tenant logins). The domains are all allowed in development but still cannot be accessed due to the port number issue. I can work around this by adding /:\d+\z/ to every allowed host, but this does not seem like a neat solution, especially since the config is Rails.application.config.hosts (you wouldn't expect this to require handling of the port). Sorry to bring up more problems but I think this one is worth resolving as it is likely to cause confusion for developers long into the future when setting up Rails.application.config.hosts if it remains as is.

@jcrisp can you send a patch or failing tests? Maybe we can support it, but from a security perspective I want to proceed cautiously. This is the third CVE we've had in the same piece of code and I'm not eager to add another.
Probably not a big deal, but http://127.0.0.1:3000/ and http://0.0.0.0:3000/ used to work, and now are blocked.
